parts.explanation: Standard column addition.
Standard column subtraction.
34÷6=5 r4, bring down 8 to make 48÷6=8.
Common denominator 42: 6/7=36/42, 1/6=7/42, difference=29/42.
Convert to improper fraction: 8/3 ÷ 1/3 = 8/3 × 3/1 = 8. Dividing by 1/3 is the same as multiplying by 3.
Work out each bracket first: 12×5=60, 24÷3=8, then 60÷8=7.5. BIDMAS/BODMAS - brackets before the outer division.

parts.text: Millimetres in 3.12m
parts.explanation: 1m=1000mm, multiply by 1000.

parts.text: Rectangular area paved with exactly 500 slabs (1m² each) - find X,Y closest to a square
parts.explanation: List factor pairs of 500 (1×500, 2×250, 4×125, 5×100, 10×50, 20×25) and pick the pair closest to equal, since a square-ish rectangle has its two sides as close to each other as possible. 20×25 is the closest pair to √500≈22.4.

parts.text: Average (mean) of 3/4 and 4/5
parts.explanation: Common denominator 20: 3/4=15/20, 4/5=16/20, sum=31/20, divide by 2 (multiply by 1/2): 31/40.
Common denominator 16: 8/16+2/16+1/16=11/16.

parts.text: Game: 7pts/goal, 3pts/penalty. 1,2,4,5,8 impossible - next lowest impossible score
parts.explanation: Systematically check each number from 9 upward for a valid combination of 7a+3b (a,b≥0 whole numbers). 9=3×3 ✓, 10=7+3 ✓, 11: 11-7=4 (not divisible by 3), 11-3=8,5,2 (none divisible by 7 cleanly) - no combination works, so 11 is impossible.

parts.text: Lowest score achievable two different ways
parts.explanation: List achievable scores with their combinations and look for the first repeat: 21 = 3 goals+0 penalties (7×3=21) or 0 goals+7 penalties (3×7=21) - two genuinely different combinations, and it's the smallest number where this happens.

parts.text: 42 = 6 goals or 14 penalties - find another combination
parts.explanation: Since 7 and 3 are the point values, trade 7 goal-points for 3+3+... penalty-points systematically: reducing goals by 1 (losing 7 points) and adding 7/3 penalties doesn't divide evenly, but reducing goals from 6 to 3 (losing 21 points) and adding 7 penalties (gaining 21 points) balances exactly: 3×7 + 7×3 = 21+21=42.

parts.text: B=2A, 2C=A, A+B+C=7 - find A
parts.explanation: Express everything in terms of C: A=2C, B=2A=4C. Sum: 2C+4C+C=7C=7, so C=1, A=2C=2.

parts.text: Find C
parts.explanation: From the working above, C=1 directly.

parts.text: 6n-2 table; two missing values (at n=8 and n=15)
parts.explanation: Substitute each given n into 6n-2: 6×8-2=46, 6×15-2=88.

parts.text: Formula n²+3, value when n=11
Machine: x4, +6, halve. Input=36 - find output
Output=163 - find input
parts.explanation: Reverse in opposite order: double (163×2=326), subtract 6 (326-6=320), divide by 4 (320÷4=80).

parts.text: Find a negative input where output equals input
parts.explanation: Set up algebraically: if x is the input, output=(4x+6)/2=2x+3. Setting x=2x+3 gives -x=3, so x=-3. Check: -3×4=-12, +6=-6, halved=-3 ✓.

parts.text: X rounds to 350 (nearest 10) - largest possible X
parts.explanation: Rounding to the nearest 10 means the true value is within 5 of 350, so the range is 345 to 354 (355 would round to 360). Largest whole number is 354.

parts.text: Y rounds to 320 - smallest possible Y
parts.explanation: Range is 315 to 324. Smallest is 315.

parts.text: Largest possible X+Y
parts.explanation: For the largest sum, use the largest possible value of each: X=354, Y=324, sum=678.

parts.text: Smallest possible X-Y
parts.explanation: For the smallest difference, use the smallest X and the largest Y: X=345, Y=324, difference=21. Trap: using the largest X and smallest Y gives the largest difference, the opposite of what's asked.

parts.text: 600cm3 petrol travels 8km - distance on 2100cm3
parts.explanation: 2100÷600=3.5 times the petrol, so 3.5×8km=28km.

parts.text: Litres needed to travel 100km
parts.explanation: 100km is 12.5 times 8km, so petrol needed=12.5×600cm³=7500cm³=7.5 litres (since 1000cm³=1 litre).

parts.text: Jenna: 7 attempts, mean=13 - total of all scores
parts.explanation: Total = mean × count = 13×7=91.

parts.text: 8th attempt scores 21 - new average
parts.explanation: New total=91+21=112, new count=8, new average=112÷8=14.

parts.text: Isosceles triangle, X=30° - find Y
parts.explanation: In an isosceles triangle the two base angles are equal. If X is the apex angle (30°), the two base angles share the remaining 150° equally: 75° each.

parts.text: If Y=81° - find X
parts.explanation: If both base angles are 81°, they sum to 162°, leaving 180-162=18° for the apex angle X.

parts.text: Three lines meet at a point (angles a, 2a, 2a) - find a
parts.explanation: Angles round a full point sum to 360°: a+2a+2a=5a=360, so a=72.

parts.text: True or false: all prime numbers are odd
parts.explanation: 2 is prime and even - a single counterexample makes 'all' false.

parts.text: True or false: some square numbers are even
parts.explanation: 4, 16, 36 are all square and even - true by example.

parts.text: True or false: some square numbers are prime
parts.explanation: Any square number n² (for n>1) has at least three factors (1, n, n²), so it can never be prime. n=1 gives 1, which isn't prime either. So no square number is ever prime - false.

parts.text: True or false: average of two odd numbers is always even
parts.explanation: Two odd numbers always sum to an even number, but dividing that even sum by 2 doesn't always give an even result - e.g. 1 and 5 average to 3 (odd). So 'always even' is false.

parts.text: Coat £64, sale 15% off + loyalty 10% off - what Mr Brown expected to pay (i.e. as if 25% off)
parts.explanation: 25% of £64 = £16, so expected price = £64-£16 = £48.

parts.text: Actual: shop gives 10% off the sale price, not original - what he actually paid
parts.explanation: Apply the discounts one after another, not added together: £64×0.85=£54.40 (after 15% off), then ×0.9=£48.96 (after a further 10% off). This is why successive discounts give a different result to a single combined percentage.

parts.text: Museum bar chart Mon-Fri - total visitors first 5 days
parts.explanation: Read each day's bar height off the chart and add the five values together.

parts.text: Average visitors Wed/Thu/Fri
parts.explanation: Add the three days' values from the chart, divide by 3.

parts.text: Tickets £2 Mon-Fri, £2.50 Sat/Sun - total ticket sales over 7 days
parts.explanation: Read each day's visitor count from the chart, multiply weekday counts by £2 and weekend counts by £2.50, then sum all seven days' revenue.

parts.text: 17.5% of X is 70 - find X
parts.explanation: 70 ÷ 0.175 = 400. Divide the given amount by the decimal form of the percentage to find the whole.

parts.text: Rectangle ABCD (B at (2,6)) rotated 90° clockwise about C - new coordinates of B
parts.explanation: Track B's position relative to the centre of rotation C, then apply the 90° clockwise rotation rule (swap coordinates and adjust signs based on direction) to find its new position.

parts.text: Rotated a further 90° clockwise - new coordinates of B
parts.explanation: Apply the same 90° clockwise rotation again to the result of the first rotation - two 90° turns together make a 180° rotation about C from the original position.

parts.text: 5 cube nets (A-E) with 3 shaded sides - which one differs from all others when folded
parts.explanation: Mentally fold each net into a cube and note which three faces end up shaded and how they relate to each other (adjacent vs. opposite). Four of the five nets fold to the same relative shading pattern; one breaks the pattern.

parts.text: Morning train Borchester 08:40 to Dryden 11:14 - duration
parts.explanation: 08:40 to 11:00 is 2hr20min, plus the remaining 14min to 11:14 = 2hr34min.

parts.text: Difference between morning and afternoon Ister-Eccleford leg durations
parts.explanation: Morning leg: 09:33 to 10:25 = 52min. Afternoon leg: 16:12 to 17:01 = 49min. Difference = 52-49 = 3min.

parts.text: Time spent in Ister taking morning train there then afternoon train onward
parts.explanation: Arrive Ister on the morning train at 09:33, depart on the afternoon train at 16:12. Time between = 6hr39min.

parts.text: Electrifying Borchester-Ister cuts time by 20% - new afternoon duration
parts.explanation: Current afternoon Borchester-Ister leg: 15:22 to 16:12 = 50min. Cut by 20%: 50×0.8=40min.

parts.text: Two shapes same perimeter - find x
parts.explanation: Write each shape's perimeter as an algebraic expression, set them equal, and solve for x.

parts.text: Two rectangles same area - find y
parts.explanation: Write each rectangle's area as an algebraic expression (length×width), set them equal, and solve for y.

parts.text: Two rectangles same area - find z
parts.explanation: Same method as above; this one has two valid solutions (z=5 and the trivial z=0), worth checking whether the equation factors to reveal both roots.

parts.text: Jack thinks of a number, multiplies by 17, gets 153 - original number
parts.explanation: Reverse the operation: 153÷17=9.

parts.text: Pippa thinks of a positive number; ×6 gives the same as squaring it - original number
parts.explanation: Set up algebraically: 6n = n², so n²-6n=0, n(n-6)=0. This gives n=0 or n=6 - since the number is positive, n=6.
